title: Advance more drugs for China’s aquaculture | Science
description: China operates the world’s largest aquaculture industry. In 2024, cultured aquatic production reached 60.6 million tonnes, accounting for 82.4% of national output and about 56% of global aquaculture production (1, 2). As farming intensifies and waters warm, disease outbreaks are becoming more frequent and complex, and farmers increasingly need effective, sustainable therapeutics that keep aquatic animals healthy and seafood safe for consumers. However, despite the industry’s scale, only 133 legally registered national-standard drugs and vaccines are available domestically for use in aquatic species (3), compared with about 2000 registered veterinary drugs for livestock and poultry (4). This portfolio cannot maintain the health and sustainability of China’s commercially farmed aquatic species.
